newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast bans timber felling.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast bans timber felling.

text.p: Ivory Coast has banned timber felling in all concessions, an official statement said.
The Forestry Ministry statement said the order came into effect on January 2, 1997.

Any company which does not have official consent to restart felling or a certificate proving it satisfies all conditions required by the official forestry concession manual, is barred from any logging within its concession.

Ivorian President Henri Konan Bedie banned log exports for 35 species on September 5, 1995 but authorised a temporary transition period which expired last December 31. The ministerial statement confirms that this ban will be extended.

"Transitional measures concerning felling and exports expired on Tuesday 31 December 1996," the statement said," adding that, a ban on exports of unhewn, square timber and boules came into effect therafter on January 2.
Concession owners will be permitted to evacuate any wood felled during the transitional period, but must obtain authorisation from the Ministry of Water and Forests.
